source.title: The Geometry of Multi-Task Grokking: Transverse Instability, Superposition, and Weight Decay Phase Structure

record.file_problem: Whole paper and appendices are present; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: Tracks train-time generalization on small modular-arithmetic tasks, using grokking steps and test accuracy, while extending the setting to shared-trunk multi-task models and adding geometric measurements.
record.gate_note: The paper reports grokking steps by task, seed, and weight decay, and reports commutator-defect onset before grokking. It also reports gradient-deletion experiments; selected endpoint and baseline conditions are recorded below, while intermediate deletion levels are noted under rows_left_out. The study does not sweep training-set size.
record.test_reason: The study measures delayed test generalization in small modular-arithmetic Transformers using training trajectories and accuracy thresholds. Its multi-task extension also tests whether geometric progress signals precede generalization.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate but incomplete. The authors interpret multi-task grokking as a geometric transition with weight-decay-dependent dynamics, defect onset preceding generalization, and no-decay failure within budget. They further propose that generalizing structure accumulates in small transverse directions, occupies a compact but distributed parameter subspace, and can use redundant optimization pathways. These mechanistic interpretations exceed direct identification of algorithms or circuit-efficiency competition.
record.recipe_differences: Uses modular arithmetic and train/test accuracy over training, but trains shared-trunk dual-task and tri-task Transformers rather than the single-task setting discussed in the original work; it also adds a weight-decay sweep and geometric measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: Grokking timescale changes with weight decay; λ = 0 runs do not grok within the stated extended budgets. The timing also differs across tasks in tri-task runs.

fits_no_version.finding: Weight decay changes grokking times, curvature, and trajectory reconstruction dimensionality; zero-decay controls do not generalize within budget.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In these small modular-arithmetic Transformers, weight decay regulates the occurrence and timing of generalization; these measurements do not identify circuit-efficiency competition.

fits_no_version.finding: Runs share attention-operator phase portraits and nearly orthogonal task heads.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Multi-task grokking exhibits recurring geometric signatures across seeds, without establishing the same implemented algorithm.

record.problems: The experiments use small Transformers (∼300k parameters), modular arithmetic mod 97, and 3 seeds for the weight-decay sweep. The paper does not test training-set-size effects. Its orthogonal-deletion experiments use one seed and one weight-decay value, and some reported grok steps use a 90% test-accuracy threshold despite a separate 98%-for-three-evaluations definition of grokking.
record.rows_left_out: The 8 defect-onset rows R61–R68 are included below the 60-row limit was not exceeded; however, the identifiers R61–R68 are not present in the rows array. Detailed orthogonal-gradient deletion results (Tables 10–11 and 16–17), PCA reconstruction thresholds (Tables 8–9 and 14–15), and other geometric measurements were not extracted because the row limit was reserved for per-task grok-step results and defect-onset results most directly tied to the tested versions.

untested.parts: Training-set-size dependence: the split is fixed at 50/50. Numerical training-accuracy saturation times and train–test delay lengths are not tabulated.

An identifiable generalizing algorithm forming gradually, removal of identifiable memorizing components, and Fourier-circuit development are not directly measured. Geometric precursors provide narrower evidence.
Non-algorithmic datasets, initialization-scale or weight-norm interventions, and a lazy-to-rich transition are not tested.
No realistic-data LLM pretraining or fine-tuning.

No comparison of generalizing versus memorizing circuit efficiency or norms, critical dataset-size prediction, or ungrokking experiment. Weight-decay dependence alone does not distinguish this account.
No identification and comparison of implemented algorithms across runs, architectures, or hyperparameters. Shared geometric signatures do not establish algorithm identity.
No optimizer, precision, or softmax numerical controls establishing whether delayed generalization disappears.

missing.what: The claimed R61–R68 do not exist. Add defect-onset versus grokking results: Table 5 reports dual-task mean leads of 6,533, 800, 9,067, 27,400, and 68,467 steps across the five nonzero decay values; all 15 conditions have positive leads. Tri-task text reports 27/27 positive leads. Figure 27 gives onset 3,700 versus grokking 162,900 for addition, seed 42, decay 0.1.
Add attention spectral-gap opening and commutator-transition timing relative to generalization, including no-decay controls. Treat these as geometric precursors rather than identified algorithms.

Add rolling-window spectral progress results: g23 declines before grokking in 18/18 successful runs versus 1/18 no-decay controls, with reported mean decline 39-fold. Resolve the tri-task task-name discrepancy before extracting subjects.
Add single-task failures for a²+ab+b² and a³+ab modulo 97: neither groks within 200,000 steps at decay 1.0, and neither shows the reported g23 decline.

record.verdict_notes: All 60 recorded numerical grok-step values match their cited tables. Grok step means first reaching 90% test accuracy; successful grokking separately requires 98% for three evaluations. Do not conflate these thresholds. The source has internal inconsistencies: Table 6 mean leads do not equal its displayed mean grok minus onset values; its 82.2%, 76.5%, 96.7% sequence is not monotonic. Table 13 names the tri-task setting add+mul+sub, whereas the main setup uses add+mul+quadratic sum. Claimed universal task ordering also has exceptions in Tables 1–2. Reconstruction and deletion results were explicitly declared omitted, so they are not listed as undeclared missing rows.

versions.untested_parts: No training-set-size sweep, so the claim that smaller training sets require more optimization is not tested. The paper defines a grok step by test accuracy, but does not give a numerical training-accuracy saturation time.

The paper tests whether commutator-defect onset anticipates generalization, but does not identify a Fourier algorithm or directly track memorizing components being removed. The gradient-deletion results do not directly measure those named components.
No non-algorithmic data or initialization-scale sweep.
No LLM pretraining or realistic-data fine-tuning.
Weight decay and its association with grokking are tested, but the paper does not sweep dataset size or test a critical dataset-size threshold or ungrokking below it.
The paper does not establish whether different runs converge to the same identifiable algorithm.
No controlled comparison of adaptive optimizers, numerical precision, or softmax floating-point effects.
